newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hogs Thursday sold steady to up $0.50 per cwt early, supported by continued strong packer demand and light marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs traded steady to up $0.50, in a range of $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants.

Illinois buyers said hogs were trading steady, but had a firm tone, with country stations paying $56.00 to $57.50 and plants $57.50 to $58.00. Indiana/Ohio top prices ranged from $55.00 to $56.00/country and $57.00 to $58.00/plants.
Prices were expected to be supported by Wednesday's higher pork prices, led by loins, butts and trimmings, which offset steady to weak skinless ham prices, sources said.
Estimated gross cutout values Wednesday were up $0.60 to $0.64 per cwt, with the number two carcass cutout up $0.62 at $78.82, USDA reported.

Light marketings also were seen underpinning prices, but scattered rainfall Wednesday and early Thursday in the Corn Belt could cause pockets of heavy numbers if producers had to abandon fieldwork temporarily, market sources said.
